units.function: open from a concept whose attention is rising

original_instantiations: The notion of large-scale records has drawn steadily greater notice in recent years as information tools have advanced.

units.function: raise the subject to a decisive fork

original_instantiations: In the age of record science, this is the fork that decides whether a firm pulls ahead or falls behind.

units.function: draw the modelling requirement out of the components

original_instantiations: The core of a firm's business is its people, its tools and its procedures. So a model for judging the system has to reckon with all three and with the links between them.
Three parts, plus the links: anything less misses the system.

prohibited_generalizations: Do not call crucial what the model omits.

original_instantiations: The edges mark a cascade between two copies, so we take the average degree as the measure of the cascade level.
A network statistic stands in for the cascade.

units.source_excerpt: The edges indicate a cascade between two data, thus we utilize the network average degree as a metric to quantify the cascade level.
units.reusable_pattern: [The structure] indicate [the meaning], thus we utilize [the statistic] as a metric to quantify [the level].
reusable_elements: occurrences: cascade section.
stable function: justify a proxy measure.
pattern: thus we utilize / as a metric to quantify.
boundary: the statistic must track the meaning.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use a statistic that measures something else.

units.function: collapse several rates into one and elevate what remains

original_instantiations: We take the transit rates through the software to be equal, so the number of hops a copy needs becomes the thing that matters.
Equal rates leave only the path length.

units.source_excerpt: We assume that rates of data transiting through computer software are the same, then the number of copy data skipping to find the real data play an important role.
units.reusable_pattern: We assume that [the rates] are the same, then [the remainder] play an important role.
reusable_elements: occurrences: cascade section.
stable function: reduce a model to one variable.
pattern: We assume that / are the same, then / play an important role.
boundary: the assumption must be stated.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop a variable silently.

units.function: claim a protocol works in two registers

original_instantiations: The rules that follow judge effectiveness in words and in numbers at once.
Both a label and a figure come out of the protocol.

units.source_excerpt: The following protocols provide effectiveness measurement both qualitatively and quantitatively.
units.reusable_pattern: The following [rules] provide [the measurement] both qualitatively and quantitatively.
reusable_elements: occurrences: protocol section.
stable function: promise both a label and a number.
pattern: both qualitatively and quantitatively.
boundary: both must be delivered.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim both if only one appears.

units.function: grade a percentage into named bands

original_instantiations: Between sixty and eighty percent the system counts as ordinarily effective, up to ninety as effective, and above that as super effective. Anything else is ineffective.
Four bands, and a residual class for the rest.

units.source_excerpt: If 60% to 80%, the system is ordinarily effective. If 80% to 90%, it is effective. If above 90, it is super effective. Otherwise, it is ineffective.
units.reusable_pattern: If [band A], [label A]. If [band B], [label B]. If [band C], [label C]. Otherwise, it is ineffective.
reusable_elements: occurrences: protocol section.
stable function: close a scale with a catch-all.
pattern: Otherwise, it is ineffective.
boundary: the bands must meet.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave a gap the catch-all hides.

units.function: send a table to a chart

original_instantiations: For a clearer view we set the scores against each other in a radar chart.
The table is restated as a picture.

units.source_excerpt: For a better presentation, in the figure, we compare them in the radar chart.
units.reusable_pattern: For a better presentation, we compare [the values] in [the chart].
reusable_elements: occurrences: demonstration section.
stable function: justify a second view of the same numbers.
pattern: For a better presentation, we compare / in.
boundary: the chart must show the same numbers.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not let the chart add numbers the table lacks.

units.function: name the weakest indicator in each group

original_instantiations: Across the three groups, the diversity of staff, the count of products and the maintenance rate score lowest, one in each.
Each group has its weakest member.

units.source_excerpt: From the aspect of people, technologies, and processes, the multi-workforce, the number of products, and the maintenance rate get the lowest points respectively.
units.reusable_pattern: From the aspect of [the groups], [the indicators] get the lowest points respectively.
reusable_elements: occurrences: demonstration section.
stable function: point at the bottleneck per group.
pattern: get the lowest points respectively.
boundary: the count must match the groups.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name a weakest indicator the chart does not show.

units.function: place a computed score on the named scale

original_instantiations: The final score comes out at 82.734, so by the table the system counts as optimizing.
The number picks its own band.

units.source_excerpt: The final maturity score is 82.734. Therefore, according to the table, this system can be considered optimizing.
units.reusable_pattern: The final [score] is [the value]. Therefore, according to [the table], [the subject] can be considered [the level].
reusable_elements: occurrences: demonstration section.
stable function: cash a number against a scale.
pattern: Therefore, according to / can be considered.
boundary: the level must be the band that contains the value.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assign a level the value misses.

units.function: claim transfer by adding indicators

original_instantiations: By adding indicators keyed to the kind of customer, the model extends readily to other firms, such as a trucking firm or a shipping firm.
New indicators, same model, new industry.

units.source_excerpt: By adding the indicators based on the customers' type, the proposed model can be easily extended and be applied to different kinds of costumers, like the trucking company and the ship company.
units.reusable_pattern: By adding [the indicators], the model can be easily extended and be applied to [the range].
reusable_elements: occurrences: benefit section.
stable function: argue transfer through extension.
pattern: can be easily extended and be applied to.
boundary: the added indicators must be specified.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim an extension that is not shown.

units.function: state the adoption condition

original_instantiations: Everyone knows that switching to a new metric is expensive. If the gain does not cover the expense, the customers will not adopt it.
Adoption hinges on the gain beating the cost.

units.source_excerpt: As is known to all, changing or building up a new metric is a high cost work. If costumers' utility cannot make up for the expenses, they won't use this metric.
units.reusable_pattern: As is known to all, [the fact]. If [the shortfall], [the actors] won't [the action].
reusable_elements: occurrences: benefit section.
stable function: set the threshold for adoption.
pattern: As is known to all / If / won't.
boundary: the model must use the threshold.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assert the fact without the condition.

units.function: split the dynamics into two cases

original_instantiations: Plainly, when the gain falls short of the cost, the customers stay away. But when the gain exceeds the cost, they may come over.
Two cases, split by one comparison.

units.source_excerpt: Apparently, if the utility is below the cost, the cost is not made up. Therefore, the costumers prefer not to use the metric. But if the utility is above the cost, the costumers may use this metric.
units.reusable_pattern: Apparently, if [case A], [the actors] prefer not to [the action]. But if [case B], [the actors] may [the action].
reusable_elements: occurrences: benefit section.
stable function: read both sides of a threshold.
pattern: Apparently, if / prefer not to. But if / may.
boundary: both cases must be analyzed.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the losing case.

units.function: read a figure into a recommendation

original_instantiations: Clearly, once the gain beats the cost the benefit climbs above every case where it does not. It climbs faster still when the cost is low. So, on this model, a gain above the cost already pays, and a lower cost pays more.
The figure says: clear the cost, then cut it.

units.source_excerpt: Obviously, when the utility exceeds the cost, the benefit goes higher than any situation when it falls short. However, the benefit increases faster with a low cost. Therefore, according to our model, once the utility is higher than the cost, the corporation obtains a high benefit.
units.reusable_pattern: Obviously, when [case A], [observation A]. However, [observation B]. Therefore, according to our model, [the conclusion].
reusable_elements: occurrences: benefit section, closing.
stable function: convert a plot into advice.
pattern: Obviously, when / However / Therefore, according to our model.
boundary: the conclusion must follow the plot.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not advise beyond the curves shown.

units.function: credit a method with two virtues

original_instantiations: The method supplies both a way of drawing the judgements out and a firm theoretical frame for exact calculation. Experts rate relative importance rather than handing over a weight directly.
Elicitation and theory, in one method.

units.source_excerpt: The method provides both an elicitation method as well as a strong theoretical framework that allows precise quantitative calculations. Instead of asking experts to directly give a weight, they will be asked to rate the relative importance.
units.reusable_pattern: [The method] provides both [virtue A] as well as [virtue B]. Instead of [the naive ask], [the better ask].
reusable_elements: occurrences: strengths.
stable function: defend a method against its crude alternative.
pattern: provides both / as well as / Instead of.
boundary: both virtues must be real.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim a framework the paper does not use.

units.function: argue transfer by what survives unchanged

original_instantiations: The model travels well. Used on another trade, most of the indicators we set down can stay as they are.
Portability means the indicators survive the move.

units.source_excerpt: The model has strong portability. To use our model in the system of other industries, most key performance indicators that we presume can be maintained.
units.reusable_pattern: The model has strong portability. To use our model in [the range], most [indicators] can be maintained.
reusable_elements: occurrences: strengths.
stable function: ground portability in reuse.
pattern: has strong portability / most / can be maintained.
boundary: the kept indicators must be named.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim portability without saying what carries over.

units.function: bound a method by what it cannot do

original_instantiations: The method can only pick the best among options that already exist, and it cannot generate a new one.
Selection, not invention.

units.source_excerpt: The method can only find the best solution from existing solutions and can not provide new solutions.
units.reusable_pattern: [The method] can only [the limited job] and can not [the missing job].
reusable_elements: occurrences: weaknesses.
stable function: state a method's ceiling.
pattern: can only / and can not.
boundary: the missing job must be real.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not imply the method does the missing job.

units.function: concede an assumption reality may break

original_instantiations: In practice the two rates could vary with time, which would make the chain non-homogeneous, and then the protocols become hard to fix.
The constant-rate assumption is the fragile part.

units.source_excerpt: The input rate and output rate could be time-varying in the real society, which leads to a nonhomogeneous Markov chain. In this situation, the effectiveness protocols are hard to determine.
units.reusable_pattern: [The quantities] could be [the complication] in the real society, which leads to [the break]. In this situation, [the deliverable] are hard to determine.
reusable_elements: occurrences: weaknesses.
stable function: name the assumption that limits the result.
pattern: could be / in the real society, which leads to / are hard to determine.
boundary: the assumption must be one the model makes.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not concede an assumption the model avoids.

units.function: open a letter with the commission and the good news

original_instantiations: Our team was brought in by the firm to measure how mature its system is. It is good to report that choosing the firm was a sound decision, since the measurement puts the system at a high level.
The commission first, the reassurance straight after.

units.source_excerpt: Our team is hired by the cooperation to measure the maturity level of their system. It is pleasant to tell you that you have made a wise decision to choose the corporation since the results take on a high-level maturity.
units.reusable_pattern: Our team is hired by [the client] to [the task]. It is pleasant to tell you that [the reassurance] since [the result].
reusable_elements: occurrences: letter, opening.
stable function: locate the writers and deliver the verdict.
pattern: Our team is hired by / It is pleasant to tell you that.
boundary: the verdict must match the result.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reassure past the evidence.

units.function: promise the reader a guided tour of the model

original_instantiations: Next we sketch the model so you can see more of how the firm's system stands.
The outline is for the reader's sake.

units.source_excerpt: We next outline our model to let you know further about the conditions of the corporation's system.
units.reusable_pattern: We next outline [the model] to let you know further about [the subject].
reusable_elements: occurrences: letter.
stable function: bridge from the verdict to the explanation.
pattern: We next outline / to let you know further about.
boundary: the outline must follow.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not promise detail the letter omits.

units.function: add the second deliverable

original_instantiations: Beyond the maturity level, we also put forward rules for judging how effective the system is.
The letter carries both deliverables.

units.source_excerpt: In addition to the system maturity level, we also propose protocols to measure its effectiveness.
units.reusable_pattern: In addition to [deliverable A], we also propose [deliverable B].
reusable_elements: occurrences: letter.
stable function: keep the second result from being lost.
pattern: In addition to / we also propose.
boundary: both deliverables must exist.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a deliverable the paper lacks.

units.function: close by praising and noting the effort continues

original_instantiations: The firm holds a system that is integrated, mature and efficient, and it is still working to improve it for a better experience.
Praise the present, then point at the ongoing effort.

units.source_excerpt: The corporation possesses an integrated, mature, and efficient system. The corporation is still trying to keep optimizing its system for a greater experience when customers using.
units.reusable_pattern: [The client] possesses an [the qualities] system. [The client] is still trying to keep optimizing [it] for [the benefit].
reusable_elements: occurrences: letter, closing.
stable function: end without claiming the work is finished.
pattern: possesses an / is still trying to keep optimizing.
boundary: the effort must be real.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not declare the system finished.

original_instantiations: Three numbered sources: a maturity-level page, a template gallery, and the original ranking report.
A short numbered list mixing web pages and a technical report.

prohibited_generalizations: Do not copy the reference list.
